records.title: revoked-artifact-accepted-as-currently-valid

proposition.statement: A relying system must not treat an artifact as currently valid after an authoritative revocation has become effective for the decision context.

preconditions: The artifact was valid before a revocation event.
An authoritative revocation became effective before the relying decision.
The relying decision asks whether the artifact is valid now.

trigger.statement: The relying system evaluates current validity using artifact evidence that does not incorporate the effective revocation state.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence establishing the artifact lifecycle state for the decision context.
Evidence that the revocation source is competent to change the artifact state.
Evidence of revocation effective time and relying decision time.
Evidence sufficient to determine that the lifecycle state is current enough for the decision.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for current validity after an authoritative revocation is known to be effective.
The system cannot establish current revocation state but converts that uncertainty into PASS.

records.title: superseded-artifact-treated-as-current

proposition.statement: A relying system must not treat a superseded artifact as the current authoritative artifact unless an explicit compatibility or historical-use rule permits that reliance.

preconditions: An artifact was previously authoritative or current.
A successor artifact or state superseded it before the relying decision.
The relying decision asks for the current authoritative artifact or state.

trigger.statement: The relying system selects or accepts the superseded artifact as current without evaluating the supersession relationship or an applicable compatibility rule.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence establishing supersession and the current artifact or state.
Evidence establishing when supersession became effective relative to the relying decision.
Any compatibility or historical-use rule that permits reliance on the superseded artifact.
Evidence linking the supersession statement to a competent source.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for current status solely from a superseded artifact when no applicable compatibility rule permits that reliance.
The system ignores known supersession evidence when selecting the current authoritative artifact.

records.title: current-withdrawal-erases-historical-validity

proposition.statement: A relying system must not infer that an artifact or event lacked historical validity merely because its authority, status, or availability was later withdrawn, revoked, or superseded.

preconditions: The artifact or event was valid under the applicable rules at historical time t1.
A later lifecycle event at time t2 changes its current status or availability.
A relying decision asks whether the artifact or event was valid at t1 rather than whether it is valid now.

trigger.statement: The relying system answers a historical-validity question using only the artifact's current withdrawn, revoked, or superseded state.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence of the artifact state at the historical time and the later lifecycle event.
Evidence distinguishing the historical verification time from the later lifecycle-event time.
Evidence of the rules governing historical validity for the relevant context.
Evidence sufficient to attribute historical and current state assertions to competent sources.

falsification.condition: The system concludes that the artifact was invalid at the historical time solely because it is withdrawn, revoked, or superseded now.
The system collapses current-state evidence and historical-state evidence into a single undifferentiated validity result.

records.title: resolved-condition-remains-blocking-after-valid-resolution

proposition.statement: A relying system must not continue to treat a material condition as unresolved after current admissible evidence positively establishes resolution under the applicable policy and authority context.

preconditions: A material condition was previously established as unresolved and blocked or deferred a consequential decision.
Current admissible evidence later satisfies the applicable resolution requirement.
The resolution evidence remains valid and current for the decision context.

trigger.statement: The relying system continues to block, defer, or report the condition as unresolved because it preserves the earlier unresolved state without reassessing current admissible evidence.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence linking the unresolved condition to the later resolution event.
Evidence that the claimed resolution remains current for the relying decision.
Evidence distinguishing the time the condition was established, the time resolution became effective, and the time of the relying decision.
Evidence that the resolution event satisfies the applicable resolution rule.
Where authority is material, evidence that the authority state supporting resolution is valid for the action and evaluation time.
Evidence showing the condition transition from unresolved to resolved or the reason it must be reopened.

falsification.condition: The system continues to block solely because the condition was once unresolved even though current admissible resolution evidence is sufficient.
A valid resolution event is ignored without evidence that it became stale, revoked, conflicting, superseded, or otherwise invalid.
The system cannot distinguish legitimate continued blocking from failure to re-evaluate the resolved condition.
